title: TensorRT-LLM: NVIDIA's LLM Compiler
description: TensorRT-LLM is NVIDIA's open-source framework for compiling large language models into optimized TensorRT engines — kernel fusion, quantization, and scheduling tuned per GPU. It serves LLMs at maximum throughput and minimum latency on NVIDIA hardware. The compiler between model and metal.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: In-Flight Batching
description: In-flight batching packs requests dynamically — new prompts join the batch as old ones finish, at the token level — keeping the GPU saturated where static batching idles. Throughput multiplies without latency exploding. Batching is the serving superpower.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: KV-Cache Management
description: The KV cache stores attention keys/values per token — TensorRT-LLM manages it with paged allocation so memory is used efficiently across the batch. Cache size bounds max context and batch. Memory planning is serving planning.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Quantization: FP8, INT8, INT4
description: TensorRT-LLM quantizes weights and activations — FP8 on Hopper, INT8/INT4 with AWQ/GPTQ — trading bits for speed at measured quality cost. Hopper's FP8 is the current sweet spot. Quantization plus compilation compounds.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Kernel Fusion and Auto-Tuning
description: The compiler fuses operations into single kernels and auto-tunes per GPU architecture — attention, norms, and MLPs become bespoke kernels. Fusion removes memory round-trips; tuning picks the fastest variant. Compiled beats generic.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Tensor and Pipeline Parallelism
description: TensorRT-LLM shards models across GPUs — tensor parallelism splits layers, pipeline parallelism splits stages — scaling past single-GPU memory. 70B+ serving is a multi-GPU compiled program. Scale is a compiler feature.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Triton Integration
description: TensorRT-LLM backends plug into NVIDIA Triton Inference Server — dynamic batching, model management, and standard APIs around the compiled engines. Triton is the serving chassis; TRT-LLM is the engine. Production serving, assembled.

title: Disaggregated Serving: Prefill vs Decode
description: Disaggregated serving splits prefill (prompt processing) from decode (generation) onto different GPUs — each phase gets the hardware shape it wants. Throughput climbs when phases stop fighting. Architecture follows the workload's two natures.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Speculative Decoding in TRT-LLM
description: TensorRT-LLM implements speculative decoding — draft model proposes, target verifies — for latency wins on top of compilation. Drafting plus compiling stacks multiplicatively. Every millisecond gets attacked.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Benchmarks: tok/s per GPU
description: TRT-LLM benchmarks quote tokens/sec per GPU, per precision, per batch — the numbers that size serving fleets. MLPerf inference includes these engines. Fleet math starts here.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-LoRA Serving
description: TensorRT-LLM serves many LoRA adapters on one base model — one engine, many personalities, with adapter switching per request. Personalization without model sprawl. The base stays shared; the adapters specialize.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Long Context Engineering
description: Long contexts (100k+ tokens) stress the KV cache — TensorRT-LLM's paged management and quantization stretch context per GPU. Context is a memory budget with engineering behind it. Long is a feature you pay for in GB.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Choosing Precision per Deployment
description: Precision choice weighs quality, speed, and hardware — FP16 for fidelity, FP8 for Hopper speed, INT4 for max throughput. The deployment's SLA picks. Measured quality deltas decide, not fashion.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
